newsitem.title: INDIA: India's hospital unit to float public issue.
newsitem.headline: India's hospital unit to float public issue.

text.p: India's Indraparastha Medical Corporation Ltd (IMCL), which runs New Delhi's Apollo Hospital, plans a public issue to raise 229 million rupees ($6.4 million) to partly finance the hospital, company officials said on Tuesday.
IMCL will enter the capital market on February 24 with ten-rupee equity shares for cash at par, a company statement said.
Prathap Reddy, the main promoter of the Apollo Hospitals Group, told reporters that the shares would be listed on the stock exchanges of Delhi, Bombay and the National Stock Exchange.
IMCL owns the Indraprastha Apollo Hospital at New Delhi, set up jointly by the Delhi government and the Apollo Hospitals Group.
The project cost of the 695-bed hospital is estimated at 18 billion rupees, to be funded by loans, lease assistance and equity.
The Delhi government will hold 26 percent equity while 25 percent will be held by the Apollo Group, the statement said.
TWL holdings Limited, a Mauritius-based company will hold 24 percent and the balance 25 percent will be held by the public. it said.
The Delhi hospital has been operational in a phased manner from April 1996. The Group also runs hospitals in the southern cities of Madras and Hyderabad. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
